model: Regulated-utility dividend discount at cost of equity with exit P/E (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: NOT revenue. FY2026E non-GAAP earnings attributable to common = guidance midpoint EPS $4.66 x 377.1M weighted diluted shares (10-Q Q3-2026 line 7873 and 7540). The 'revenue' slot carries the earnings stream; 'growth_rates' are per-share EPS growth; 'ebitda_margin_path' is the dividend payout ratio; FCF = dividends to current holders.
inputs.share_count_basis: 377,027,555 common shares outstanding 2026-10-31 (10-Q Q3-2026 cover, line 5656) plus 0.6M dilutive RSU/performance-share effect (Q3-2026 diluted 377,658,965, line 7543) = 377.7M fully diluted. Held FLAT: growth_rates are per-share EPS growth, so the $0.8-1.1B 2026-2030 ATM programme and DRIP/comp issuance are already netted inside the guided 5-7% EPS growth. Growing the count as well would charge dilution twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO by construction: the valued stream (dividends out of post-interest earnings) is already after debt service, so deducting net debt again would count the debt twice (SKILL.md: never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow). Actual consolidated net debt at 2026-09-30 is recorded below for auditability and for the leverage read.
inputs.total_debt_note: 2026-09-30 (10-Q Q3-2026 lines 5836-5853): long-term debt 26,022.9 + current portion 2,875.2 + rate reduction bonds 237.7 + RRB current 43.2 + notes payable 0 = 29,179.0 ($M). Down from 30,114 at 2025-12-31 after Aquarion proceeds (~$1.6B cash + ~$0.8B debt extinguished) were applied to debt.
inputs.last_fcf_definition: FY2026E common dividends to current holders = DPS $3.15 ($0.7875 x 4, 10-Q Q3-2026 lines 5922-5938) x 377.1M shares = $1,188M. This is the flow the model discounts. It is NOT owner FCF: ES's reported FCF (OCF - capex) was -$45M in FY2025, +$391M in H1-2026, and is structurally near zero or negative through the $26.5B 2026-2030 capital plan because growth capex is funded with debt and equity and earns a regulated return. Discounting that series would value a regulated utility at roughly nothing (see AIA.NZ memory for the same capex-supercycle trap).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back $33.6M (0.25% of revenue, 1.9% of earnings). Set to 0 in the driver paths because SBC is already expensed inside the GAAP/non-GAAP earnings stream being valued; deducting it again would double-charge. House and street bases therefore coincide and band_position is degenerate (see notes).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income $125.5M is mostly carrying charges on regulatory assets, not interest on a surplus cash pile; cash is $525M against $29.2B of debt. Not stripped: it is inside earnings and no cash pile is added back.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases; ES is a net ISSUER ($465M of common shares issued in 9M-2025 via ATM, $20M in 9M-2026; 10-Q Q3-2026 line 6019). Guidance: $800M-$1.1B of equity 2026-2030 plus DRIP/comp issuance.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.fy2026_guidance_eps_non_gaap: 4.62-4.70, midpoint 4.66 (narrowed at Q3-2026 from 4.57-4.72; original Feb-2026 guide 4.80-4.95 cut for FERC Opinion 594 transmission ROE and loss of Aquarion earnings)
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is the COST OF EQUITY, because the stream is a dividend out of post-interest earnings. USD build: 10-year UST ~4.2% (early Nov 2026) + beta 0.65-0.70 x ERP ~5.3% = 7.7-7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Cross-checks: allowed ROEs on the rate base are 9.32% (Yankee Gas, PURA Nov-2025) to 9.57% (FERC base, Opinion 594) and the market prices ES at 15.0x FY2026E EPS / 4.5% dividend yield, consistent with a 7.5-8.5% equity return expectation. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios; regulatory risk is charged in the growth and payout paths and in the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: leases are immaterial ($2M/yr interest on lease liabilities, 10-K FY2023 line 12220) and are inside operating expense within the earnings stream.
inputs.nci_treatment: Preferred stock of subsidiaries ($155.6M) and NCI are deducted before Net Income Attributable to Common Shareholders; the stream is already attributable-only.
inputs.notes: MODEL: regulated-utility dividend discount at cost of equity with an exit multiple, run through the Drivers/engine route (same pattern as the GPT.AX/GMG.AX AFFO capitalisations). dcf-methods SKILL.md has no explicit regulated-utility row; the business is a compounder of rate base at an allowed ROE, so the compounder-of-book row (BVPS compounding x exit P/B) is the nearest fit, and the dividend-discount build used here is its cash-flow equivalent (cross-check below ties within ~3%). The owner-FCF DCF was rejected because reported FCF is structurally ~zero/negative through the $26.5B capital plan (FY2025 -$45M) and would value the equity at nothing, which AIA.NZ's memory shows is a method artefact, not a finding. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue slot = earnings attributable to common (FY2026E $1,757M); growth_rates = per-share EPS growth (nets ATM dilution); ebitda_margin_path = dividend payout ratio; SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (all already inside earnings); wacc = cost of equity 8.0%; net_debt = 0 (post-interest stream); terminal_cap_multiple = 25x dividends (~16x P/E at a 64% payout), above the Gordon multiple in every scenario so Gordon binds everywhere; horizon 10 years FY2027-FY2036 because the guided 5-7% EPS growth runs to 2030 and needs a fade. HOUSE vs STREET: the earnings stream is post-SBC and SBC paths are 0, so house = street and band_position is degenerate (the engine prints 0 or null; read it as 'band collapsed', not 'price at house value'). BVPS CROSS-CHECK: BVPS $43.55 at 2026-09-30 compounding at ~4%/yr (10.7% non-GAAP ROE x 33% retention + ~0.6%/yr accretion from issuing at 1.6x book) reaches ~$64 by FY2036; at a 1.5x exit P/B (sector range 1.4-1.8x) that is ~$97, PV ~$45 at 8%, plus ~$27 PV of dividends = ~$72/share vs the base-case DDM. STALE-ANCHOR GUARD: price is a Friday regular close two days before the valuation date; balance sheet and share count are the Q3-2026 10-Q (Sept 30 / Oct 31, 2026), post-Aquarion.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 EPS growth at the lower-middle of management's reaffirmed 5-7% cumulative range off the $4.66 FY2026 base, consistent with the 5.1% GAAP / 5.9% non-GAAP 5-year EPS CAGR and the 5.9% DPS CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 2.9% diverges >30% from revenue (8.8%) and EPS (5.1%). Cause: book equity absorbed the FY2023 ~$1.95B offshore-wind impairment (GAAP net loss -$435M) and FY2024 Aquarion impairment (-$254M water segment), so equity growth understates the ~8% rate-base growth that drives regulated earnings. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth source here.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are undefined: reported FCF (OCF - capex) was negative in every year FY2017-FY2025 except FY2016, ranging from -$45M (FY2025) to -$2.69B (FY2023), because growth capex ($4.2-4.5B/yr) exceeds OCF ($1.6-4.1B). This is the normal profile of a utility in a rate-base growth phase, not distress. Revenue 3-yr CAGR is depressed by pass-through energy-supply cost swings (FY2022 $12.3B -> FY2024 $11.9B -> FY2025 $13.5B); revenue is not an earnings driver for a rate-regulated T&D utility. CAGRs: revenue FY2020 $8,904M -> FY2025 $13,547M; GAAP EPS FY2020 $3.56 -> FY2025 $4.56; equity FY2020 $14,064M -> FY2025 $16,197M; DPS FY2020 $2.27 -> FY2025 $3.01.

base.narrative: EPS grows 5.5% in FY2027 off the $4.66 base, reaching the upper half of the 5-7% range (6.5%) in FY2029-30 as management guides, then fades to 3% by FY2036 as the capital plan normalises. Payout drifts from 67% (DPS $3.15 / EPS $4.66) to 64% because dividend growth (~5%) runs slightly behind EPS growth, consistent with the 2021-2026 pattern (DPS +5.9%/yr vs non-GAAP EPS +5.9%/yr, payout 62-68%).

bull.narrative: EPS growth at or just above the top of the 5-7% range through 2030: the full $26.5B plan is deployed on schedule with constructive MA/NH PBR outcomes, the ~$700M ISO-NE-selected transmission project is added, the FERC rehearing/appeal restores part of the 100 bp base-ROE cut, and the CL&P rate case lands near the requested ROE. Payout falls to 62% as EPS outruns a ~5-6% dividend. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects a longer electrification-driven rate-base runway.

bear.narrative: EPS growth undershoots the range at ~3%: the FERC 9.57% base ROE sticks and incentive adders are trimmed further, PURA keeps disallowing storm costs (~$500M disallowed in 2026) and sets CL&P's ROE near Yankee Gas's 9.32%, higher-for-longer rates lift interest expense on $29B of debt, and the equity need rises toward/above $1.1B at a lower share price. The board defends the dividend at ~3-4% growth for several years, so payout creeps up to 70% before dividend growth is cut to the earnings pace. Terminal growth 2.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Eversource delivers the reaffirmed 5-7% EPS growth algorithm off the narrowed $4.66 FY2026 base: ~8% rate-base growth from the $26.5B 2026-2030 plan, less ~1%/yr dilution from the $0.8-1.1B ATM programme and DRIP, less modest earned-vs-allowed ROE leakage in Connecticut. The FERC Opinion 594 cut (10.57% -> 9.57% base ROE) and the PURA storm-cost disallowances are already in the FY2026 base and are assumed permanent. Dividends grow ~5%/yr, payout eases from 67% to 64%. Discounted at an 8.0% cost of equity with 3% terminal growth, the exit is ~13x FY2036 EPS, below today's 15x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Regulatory friction eases at the margin: part of the FERC ROE cut is restored on appeal, the pending CL&P rate case is constructive, MA/NH PBR mechanisms keep earned ROE near allowed, and the ~$700M of incremental ISO-NE transmission plus electrification-driven load growth extends the capital plan. EPS compounds at ~7-7.5% through 2030 and the market pays a ~15x exit. No further offshore-wind charges.
scenario_narratives.bear: Connecticut stays structurally adversarial (further storm-cost disallowances, CL&P ROE near 9.3%, PBR penalties), the FERC cut is final and incentive adders are trimmed, interest costs rise on the $29B debt stack, and the equity need grows at a lower share price. EPS growth settles at ~3% rather than 5-7%, the dividend is defended until payout reaches 70%, and a further Revolution Wind cost-sharing charge (analyst worst case >$700M) is possible but not modelled as a recurring item. Exit ~12x EPS.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the thesis depends on a single adversarial regulator (CT PURA has disallowed ~$500M of storm costs, cut Yankee Gas to 9.32% and drawn AG criticism) and the FERC ROE cut has already forced two guidance cuts in 2026; bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent outcomes (FERC appeal, CL&P rate case, on-time capex, no further offshore-wind charges) to go right at once. Base 50%: management's 5-7% algorithm has been met over 2020-2025 (non-GAAP EPS +5.9%/yr) despite the same jurisdictions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a regulated T&D utility as the stream of dividends its allowed return on a growing rate base can fund, discounted at the cost of equity, with an exit at a normal utility P/E, not as owner FCF, which is structurally negative while the $26.5B capital plan is being built and would price the equity at nothing. Earnings growth is taken from management's reaffirmed 5-7% EPS algorithm, already net of the equity issuance that funds the plan, and stress-tested against the two live regulatory frictions (FERC Opinion 594 and CT PURA). The weighted value sits close to the current price: at a 4.5% yield and 15x earnings the market is already pricing ES as a ~8% equity-return bond proxy, and the upside depends on regulatory outcomes rather than on the growth plan itself.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50 bp on the 8.0% discount rate moves the base value ~10%; a higher-for-longer 10-year UST is the single biggest swing factor
Connecticut PURA: further storm-cost disallowances, a sub-9.5% CL&P ROE or PBR penalties would push the path toward the bear case
FERC Opinion 594: the 9.57% base ROE is in the FY2026 base; a rehearing win is upside, a further incentive-adder cut is downside
Equity dilution: the $0.8-1.1B ATM is inside the 5-7% EPS guidance; a lower share price or a larger plan raises the share count faster than modelled
Residual Revolution Wind cost-sharing (2025-26 charges ~$164M+ after-tax; abandonment worst case >$700M) is excluded from the recurring stream
Terminal exit multiple: the base case exits at ~13x FY2036 EPS vs 15x today; if the sector re-rates to 17-18x the model is conservative, if to 12x it is not
